issue.body:
So @bdraco was adding new tests in https://github.com/aio-libs/multidict/pull/1072. And it worked at first. But they had readability problems, and I added a few refactoring commits on top. And that's when things went south.

The first version of the tests made use of `@pytest.mark.parametrize` which I later converted into a parametrized fixture. That specific fixture depends on `request: pytest.FixtureRequest`, but doesn't depend on anything else we have declared in `conftest.py`.

The params set uses a trick that @The-Compiler has shown in his EuroPython 2023 workshop — wrapping them in dataclasses featuring `__str__()` interface. Not sure if that's relevant, though.

I was able to reproduce it locally on my Gentoo Linux laptop using pypy3.9-7.3.16. But I wasn't really able to make the repro smaller. I learned that this traceback is first seen in `pytest == 8.2.2`. And `pytest == 8.2.1` does not have this problem.

So the current STR is something like:
1. `pyenv install pypy3.9-7.3.16`
2. `pyenv virtualenv pypy3.9-7.3.16 multidict-pyenv-pypy3.9-7.3.16`
3. `pyenv shell multidict-pyenv-pypy3.9-7.3.16`
4. Get a copy of https://github.com/aio-libs/multidict/pull/1072
5. `pip install -r requirements/pytest.txt`
6. `pip install -e .`
7. `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PYTEST='8.2.2.dev0+first-broken-due-to-pr12414-regression' pip install 'pytest @ https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/archive/214d098fcce88940f5ce9353786b3cc8f0bd3938.tar.gz'`
8. And finally run `pytest --collect-only --no-cov tests/test_abc.py tests/test_copy.py tests/test_incorrect_args.py tests/test_multidict.py tests/test_mypy.py tests/test_pickle.py tests/test_types.py tests/test_update.py tests/test_version.py`

These aren't all the test modules of the project. Removing them from CLI args or removing some of the tests inside makes it so that it doesn't traceback anymore. That's why I wasn't able to come up with a single-snippet reproducer. It feels like it only happens when a certain amount of tests is hit or something.

I also ran it with `--pdb` which allowed me to see the value of `item` at that point when `OrderedDict.move_to_end()` is called: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blame/2b40981/src/_pytest/fixtures.py#L278C29-L280C30.
It kinda suggests that the PyPy implementation of `OrderedDict` is weird:
```pycon
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> PDB post_mortem (IO-capturing turned off) >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> ~/.pyenv/versions/pypy3.9-7.3.16/envs/multidict-pyenv-pypy3.9-7.3.16/lib/pypy3.9/site-packages/_pytest/fixtures.py(236)fix_cache_order()
```

🤔 *Why* does this dict have duplicate keys? 😱

Anyway.. I confirmed that doing `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PYTEST='8.2.2.dev0+last-working-right-before-pr12414-regression' pip install 'pytest @ https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/archive/b41d5a52bbb808780ab310456d71e5ce509fd402.tar.gz'` makes the problem go away (which is expected because it does not yet have the `OrderedDict.move_to_end()` call).

And so this makes https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/pull/12414 (https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/pull/12409) responsible for the regression.

cc @bluetech I hope you'll have at least some idea of where to look because I've spent enough time staring at this w/o any clue...


---

UPD: I also forgot to mention that removing our own `pytest_collection_modifyitems` in `conftest.py` does not help in any way, it still reproduces. Plus, changing the fixture scopes to match what we have in `conftest.py` has no effect either.

UPD2: pypy3.11-7.3.19 shows this behavior too.

Unfortunately, debugging RPython is above my pay grade. It would be interesting to find out when duplicate keys get introduced, but at least at a first glance, nothing stands out. Most of the code is calling into `dict` superclass, and `move_to_end()` is literally `del` + set again.

it may be possible the exact behavior is dependent on the dictionary strategy in pypy
i wonder if there is a potential minimal testcase we can invent -

The above was the minimum I could come up with. At some point, deselecting one more test was making it work. So I gave up for the time being...

I thought that maybe it's PyPy's GC mechanism that influences this again. But I also don't know how to troubleshooting that.
My guess would be that the key to reproducing it would be figuring out how did it manage to end up with a duplicate key.
a fine hack to validate would be if using a dict plus `d[item]  =d.pop(item)`would solve it better

> My guess would be that the key to reproducing it would be figuring out how did it manage to end up with a duplicate key.

Yep, that's exactly what I can't wrap my head around. And staring at the PyPy source code has given me exactly zero clarity 🤷‍♂️

thanks everyone for trying to track this down! I'll try to understand what's going on and have two questions that would help me a lot:
- is it correct that `move_to_end` is used, and that that leads to the bug somehow?
- the keys are tuples of a number of strings and pytest internal types, correct?

It's likely that the bug managed to hide for a long time because `move_to_end` is a relatively rare operations.

move_to_end is used and the key is a pytest internal type


we use a `OrderedDict[Item, None]` as a OrderedSet[Item]

> is it correct that move_to_end is used, and that that leads to the bug somehow?

@cfbolz it is used, but I'm not entirely sure that it is the underlying cause of the issue (unless you're implying that previous invocations of this method on the same object had effect at some point in the future). When I was running pdb, I was trying to access the problematic key through normal square brackets and it was giving me the same key error. And then I listed the keys, and noticed that the problematic one was duplicated.

Okay, I'm not sure if this is something you want to do upstream, but to unblock Gentoo for the time being I'm going to apply the following hack:

```diff
diff --git a/src/_pytest/fixtures.py b/src/_pytest/fixtures.py
index 6b882fa35..985e45ce3 100644
--- a/src/_pytest/fixtures.py
+++ b/src/_pytest/fixtures.py
@@ -278,6 +278,12 @@ def reorder_items_atscope(
                     for other_scope in HIGH_SCOPES:
                         other_scoped_items_by_argkey = items_by_argkey[other_scope]
                         for argkey in argkeys_by_item[other_scope].get(i, ()):
+                            if hasattr(sys, "pypy_version_info"):
+                                # Gentoo workaround for https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13312
+                                del other_scoped_items_by_argkey[argkey][i]
+                                new_dict = OrderedDict({i: None})
+                                new_dict.update(other_scoped_items_by_argkey[argkey])
+                                continue
                             other_scoped_items_by_argkey[argkey][i] = None
                             other_scoped_items_by_argkey[argkey].move_to_end(
                                 i, last=False
```

i.e. just inline `move_to_end(last=False)` (unless I messed the logic up).

Chasing the link to the PyPy code that @RonnyPfannschmidt linked, I *think* that `move_to_end(last=False)` ends up in this code:

https://github.com/pypy/pypy/blob/f58a4aee085665550ee92f65930176d8284dae9c/rpython/rtyper/lltypesystem/rordereddict.py#L1537-L1621

It is too complex for me to figure out quickly. But I do see it contains several assertions (`ll_assert` calls). I'm assuming these assertions are turned off in a production build of PyPy, but if the bug can be reproduced under an assertions-enabled build of PyPy maybe we get lucky and one the assertions will fail.

If I get some time, I will also try to run some property tests for OrderedDict.move_to_end on PyPy, maybe we get lucky with this and find a bug...

I am also trying to read `reorder_items` again to understand if the problem might be on the pytest side, but that code is a bit of a maze (it was much worse in the past!)...

I found a shorter reproducer, see I the discussion https://github.com/pypy/pypy/issues/5257

I'm fairly close to solving it, basically move_to_first can break an invariant of the dict (which doesn't have an ll_assert 🙄).

@cfbolz Awesome! > If I get some time, I will also try to run some property tests for OrderedDict.move_to_end on PyPy, maybe we get lucky with this and find a bug... So given there is a PyPy bug (still super surprised by this, this definitely goes on the pytest Wall of Bugs, along with [this](https://bugs.python.org/issue41909) cpython crasher), maybe we should workaround it?

@mgorny

> i.e. just inline move_to_end(last=False) (unless I messed the logic up).

I'm afraid it is messed up - not doing anything with `new_dict`.

Using the "new dict and assign" strategy is problematic because the type of `other_scoped_items_by_argkey` is `Mapping` which doesn't allow mutation (even though it's actually a dict, type checker will complain). This is a property I'd like to preserve. So I think we want a "backup, clear and update" strategy. That's a bit gruesome but I at least can't think of a more efficient alternative to `move_to_end(last=False)`. I will send a PR.
